title: Phone: DFPC Proposes Unified Command, Coyote Draw Fire

fields.orgName: Sawmill County Office of Emergency Management

caller.name: Duty Officer Marcus Lindqvist
caller.label: Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control, Northeast Region

callee.name: Chief Dwight Kowalski
callee.label: Pine Gulch Fire Protection District, on speaker at the Sawmill County EOC with Emergency Manager Elena Marchetti

transcript.speaker: Chief Dwight Kowalski
transcript.text: Pine Gulch Battalion 1, you're on speaker in the county EOC. Emergency Manager Elena Marchetti is with me. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: DFPC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Chief, Marcus Lindqvist, DFPC Northeast Region duty officer. I have your 15:20 size-up: Coyote Draw Fire, 1,100 acres, zero percent, with spotting into PG-03. That's beyond district capacity. DFPC will take the fire lead as soon as you agree. We propose a Unified Command with the Sheriff, run out of the Pine Gulch EOC.

transcript.speaker: DFPC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Our incident commander trainee arrives at 16:15. Before then we need three answers from you and the Sheriff. Who runs the Evacuation Branch? Who runs the traffic control points? And who signs off on acreage and containment before anything goes out to the public? Right now we're hearing 800, 1,100, and twelve hundred from the media.

transcript.speaker: Chief Dwight Kowalski
transcript.text: Understood. Stand by. I'm conferencing in interagency dispatch for the resource picture.

transcript.speaker: Northern Colorado Interagency Dispatch
transcript.text: EOC, Northern Colorado Interagency Dispatch, resource order status as of 15:32. Type 3 engine strike team ST-CO-4417 is en route, ETA 16:20. Two SEATs are committed out of the Fort Collins-Loveland tanker base, first drop at about 15:55.

transcript.speaker: Northern Colorado Interagency Dispatch
transcript.text: Your Type 1 helicopter request is UTF, unable to fill. The national preparedness level is 3 and there are no Type 1 ships available in the region today.

transcript.speaker: Northern Colorado Interagency Dispatch
transcript.text: One more thing. The county request for one bus and three ambulances for Stonebridge Assisted Living is still showing open. Nobody has acknowledged it on our end. Do you still need it, and who is the contact?

transcript.speaker: DFPC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Chief, EOC, I'll call back at 15:50 for your answer on the command structure. If the county is thinking about a state declaration or an FMAG request, tell me now and I'll start the paperwork on our side.

voiceStyles.DFPC Duty Officer: Man in his 50s, calm and businesslike state fire officer, steady pace, slight radio-room echo
voiceStyles.Northern Colorado Interagency Dispatch: Woman in her 30s, brisk dispatcher cadence, reads the list without pausing, busy room behind her
voiceStyles.Chief Dwight Kowalski: Man in his 40s, clipped and winded, calling from a vehicle with wind noise

instructorNote: This call tests how the EOC sets up command: the Fire Chief and the Sheriff should form Unified Command (EOP 3). The Sheriff keeps evacuation authority. The Undersheriff keeps the Evacuation Branch and the traffic control points, with sweep reports every 15 minutes (SENTCS 3, step 4). Acreage and containment should come only from the IC, with a time stamp. Watch whether the EM re-requests the unacknowledged bus and ambulances for Stonebridge (EOP 5, item 6) and starts the state declaration and FMAG requests (EOP 5, item 7).
